title: Being put on second and refused as a follow-up act
summary: Black girls were not accepted in smart clothes and were put on second to liven the bill; one white performer refused to follow her.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: How did you and the other black$ -- how did you feel about that, at that time?

Well, of course we resented it, but we wanted to get on big time. So when you want to do something, you accept what you can get until you're in a position to speak out. So we didn't think it was fair, because most of the white girls would come and ask us how we did such and such a thing, you understand. And then several places -- theaters I went, they had me on the stage just -- they'd always put us on second, see, to liven things up for the rest of them.

But, oh, Lord, I have it written down some place, one of the white performers refused to follow me. She said she couldn't follow me. So they had to take me off of second. She refused to follow me. Because instead of making it hot for her, I made it too hot. So they took me off. I have all that down, I think, in a book. And they -- this girl refused to follow me. So now what else?
